items.informal_name: Compatibility of Partial Derivatives with Renaming in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} [inst : CommSemiring R] {τ : Type u_1} {f : σ → τ},
  Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (x : σ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
      (MvPolynomial.pderiv (f x)) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p) = (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv x) p)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative semiring, $ \sigma, \tau $ be variable index sets, and $ f : \sigma \to \tau $ an injective map. For any polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $ and variable $ x \in \sigma $, the partial derivative operator commutes with renaming variables via $ f $: $ \frac{\partial}{\partial (f(x))} (p^f) = (\frac{\partial p}{\partial x})^f $, where $ p^f $ denotes the polynomial obtained by renaming variables according to $ f $.

items.informal_name: Partial Derivative of Sum Iteration Equals Sum of Partial Derivatives in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} (p : MvPolynomial (σ ⊕ ι) R) (i : σ),
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) ((MvPolynomial.sumToIter R σ ι) p) =
    (MvPolynomial.sumToIter R σ ι) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl i)) p)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, types $ \sigma $ and $ \iota $, and polynomial $ p $, the partial derivative with respect to variable $ i $ of the $ \text{sumToIter} $ representation of $ p $ is equal to the $ \text{sumToIter} $ of the partial derivatives of each term of $ p $ with respect to the left-injected variable $ i $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Preservation Under Injective Variable Renaming in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ),
  Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : σ →₀ ℕ),
      MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.mapDomain f d) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ) = MvPolynomial.coeff d φ
items.informal_description: For an injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, a multivariate polynomial $ \varphi \in R[\sigma] $, and a finite support function $ d : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $, the coefficient of the monomial $ d.\text{mapDomain}(f) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(f, \varphi) $ equals the coefficient of $ d $ in $ \varphi $. This holds because injective renaming preserves monomial coefficients when variables are relabeled without collision.

items.informal_name: Injective Variable Renaming Preserves Homogeneous Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] {φ : MvPolynomial σ R} {n : ℕ} {f : σ → τ},
  Function.Injective f → (((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ).IsHomogeneous n ↔ φ.IsHomogeneous n)
items.informal_description: Given an injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, a multivariate polynomial $ \varphi $ is homogeneous of degree $ n $ if and only if the polynomial obtained by renaming its variables via $ f $ is homogeneous of degree $ n $.

items.informal_name: Injective Renaming Preserves Variable Degree in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : MvPolynomial σ R} {f : σ → τ},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ (i : σ), MvPolynomial.degreeOf (f i) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p) = MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for any injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, the total degree of the variable $ f(i) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \operatorname{rename}(f, p) $ equals the total degree of the variable $ i $ in the original polynomial $ p $. Symbolically, $ \deg_{f(i)}(\operatorname{rename}(f, p)) = \deg_i(p) $.
